title: Light–Dark Circadian Entrainment
mission: Synchronise the central circadian clock with the external light–dark cycle through retinal light signals.
rationale: Prior circadian reassessment distinguishes melatonin suppression from phase entrainment. No dietary input established; unselected light protocols are outside this food abstraction. Retain as a current no-new-dietary-lever assessment.

title: Feeding-Time Circadian Synchronisation
mission: Coordinate peripheral metabolic clock timing through feeding cues.
rationale: Feeding-related peripheral entrainment is distinct from retinal central-clock entrainment. Reuse bounded phase evidence; do not convert a phase shift into a beneficial dietary effect.

title: NAPE → NAE Biosynthesis Capacity
mission: Enable NAPE-to-NAE biosynthesis so endocannabinoidome signalling lipids remain available for stress and motivation regulation.
rationale: Prior bounded assessment does not establish that ordinary dietary NAPE/PE supplies brain NAE synthesis; precursor pool, tissue delivery and enzyme engagement remain separate.

title: Omega-3-Derived Endocannabinoidome Signalling
mission: Sustain omega-3-derived ethanolamide production so endocannabinoidome neuromodulation stays supplied from dietary fat status.
rationale: Omega-3 ethanolamide formation is not interchangeable with EPA/DHA membrane supply or generic fish effects. No independently verified food-to-PM ethanolamide effect selected.

title: FAAH-Mediated Endocannabinoid Preservation
mission: Preserve endocannabinoid signalling duration by limiting FAAH-mediated degradation of anandamide and related NAEs.
rationale: Isolated FAAH pharmacology does not establish ordinary dietary inhibition. Preserve prior no-admission assessment.

title: Endocannabinoid–Dopamine Neuromodulation
mission: Shape dopaminergic reward and motivation pathways through endocannabinoid neuromodulatory interaction.
rationale: Endocannabinoid effects on dopamine/reward do not identify a supported food exposure. Preserve prior no-admission assessment.

title: Endocannabinoid Stress-Buffering Capacity
mission: Sustain endocannabinoid-mediated stress buffering so HPA-axis and neuroinflammatory reactivity stay proportionate.
rationale: Exercise/stress evidence cannot be abstracted as food effects; ECS mediation and dietary exposure have not passed this run’s gate.

title: Oestrogen Signalling Stability
mission: Maintain stable oestrogen-linked signalling so dopamine tone and emotional regulation remain steady across hormonal fluctuation.
rationale: Fibre-associated circulating oestrogen changes do not establish stable brain oestrogen signalling. Matrix, population and mechanism require separate attribution.

title: Estrobolome Regulation
mission: Shape systemic oestrogen exposure through microbiome-mediated regulation of oestrogen metabolism and recycling.
rationale: Bacterial beta-glucuronidase activity and oestrogen recirculation do not independently establish a dietary regulator of this PM; retain prior unresolved assessment.

title: Progesterone-Supportive Microbial Metabolism
mission: Sustain microbial contributions to progesterone-related hormonal stability through gut ecosystem function.
rationale: Microbial progestin conversion is not equivalent to progesterone support or brain neurosteroid exposure; mission/ownership and directional interpretation require review.

title: Metabolic-Reproductive Hormone Integration
mission: Enable coordinated integration of insulin and metabolic signalling with reproductive hormone balance.
rationale: Low-GI PCOS programme evidence is population- and intervention-specific. Insulin/theca biology does not independently validate a generic hormone-balancing diet.

title: Testosterone Signalling Stability
mission: Maintain androgen receptor signalling so motivation, stamina, and goal-directed effort remain well supported.
rationale: Serum testosterone after sleep or zinc manipulation is not a direct measure of androgen-receptor signalling stability. No food efficacy claim admitted.

title: Androgen-Microbiome Regulation
mission: Shape systemic androgen exposure through microbiome-mediated androgen metabolism and recycling.
rationale: Local microbial androgen deconjugation is distinct from systemic or brain exposure; food-to-activity relationship remains unverified.

title: Amino-Acid Availability & Prioritisation
mission: Ensure meal-level protein supply delivers the amino-acid foundation neurotransmitter pathways depend on.
rationale: Established amino-acid provision retained historically. Aggregate indispensable-AA/protein identities, six missing individual EAA composition mappings and formulation/digestibility attribution prevent complete rapid food abstraction of this pool.

title: LAT1 Competitive Transport Modulation
mission: Influence competition for transport across the blood–brain barrier so neurotransmitter precursors can reach the brain after meals.
rationale: Historical meal carbohydrate/protein pattern admission conflicts with current section-specific eligibility. Plasma LNAA ratios are not measured brain LAT1 flux. Withhold this pattern from §3.1.1; no automatic SOP transfer.

title: Dopaminergic Signalling Regulation
mission: Maintain appropriately regulated dopamine synthesis, storage, release, receptor signalling, reuptake and metabolism across changing functional demand.
rationale: Tyrosine/cofactor capacity is distinct from dopamine signalling and inverted-U effects. Source-specific reaction, dietary precursor and brain flux attribution not fully verified in this run; no extrapolated food dopamine effect.

title: Noradrenergic Signalling
mission: Support noradrenergic alertness and executive control so attention and arousal stay appropriately engaged.
rationale: Retain historical noradrenaline-related capacity decisions; review separates precursor/PLP supply from actual norepinephrine synthesis/release. Exact receptor/state and dietary exposure claims deferred.

title: Serotonergic Signalling Regulation
mission: Support serotonergic signalling so mood stability, inhibition, and behavioural regulation remain well grounded.
rationale: Tryptophan provision, LAT1 competition, TPH2 flux and serotonin signalling are separate. Current corpus includes bibliographic gaps; no unverified serotonin food claim exported.

title: Acetylcholine Synthesis Support
mission: Maintain the capacity to form acetylcholine so cholinergic signalling for attention, working memory, and learning stays supplied.
rationale: ChAT/neuronal substrate supply is distinct from PC membrane biosynthesis. B5/folate context and shared-pool claims are retained but not promoted.

title: Neuronal Membrane DHA Incorporation
mission: Deliver and integrate DHA into neuronal membranes so the brain maintains a flexible, signal-ready lipid foundation.
rationale: Owns DHA incorporation, not choline methyl-donor limitation or downstream clinical effects; those associated donor claims remain unresolved for this run.

title: Glutamate Clearance & Recycling
mission: Clear and recycle glutamate efficiently so excitatory load does not overwhelm neural circuits.
rationale: Current bounded Stage 2B admits no clearance-specific dietary requirement. Magnesium NMDA effects belong to a different operation; no lever imported.

title: Excitotoxicity Modulation
mission: Limit excitotoxic pressure when glutamatergic drive is excessive so neural stability is protected over time.
rationale: Current Stage 2B parks isolated-model magnesium-sulfate protection and generic antioxidants/omega-3 as unresolved; ordinary-food excitotoxic protection not established.

title: GABA Synthesis Capacity
mission: Maintain sufficient glutamate decarboxylase capacity, and sufficient PLP cofactor to support it, so GABA can be synthesised from glutamate.
rationale: Specific GAD capacity is distinct from GABA concentration, receptor outcomes and the neighbouring glutamate-cycle mechanisms. Reuse existing B6 admission with explicit activation and exposure limits.

title: Synaptic Structural Plasticity
mission: Maintain and adapt physical connections between neurons through synapse formation, selective stabilisation, structural remodelling and elimination.
rationale: Recent bounded assessment preserves synaptic structure versus membrane incorporation. Combined choline/uridine/DHA exposures, age/model and human delivery need exact attribution before food-specific structural claims.

title: Folate/B12-Dependent Homocysteine Remethylation
mission: Recycle homocysteine to methionine through folate and B12 so methyl-donor supply and homocysteine control stay supported.
rationale: MTR remethylation is distinct from BHMT, MAT and transsulfuration. Reuse the supported capacity pathways, not a claim that lower blood homocysteine measures brain remethylation.

title: Betaine/BHMT Remethylation
mission: Provide a parallel homocysteine clearance route so methionine and SAMe supply remain resilient when folate demand is high.
rationale: BHMT remethylation has separate enzyme and tissue ownership from MTR; betaine chemistry is not a direct neurotransmitter or clinical outcome.

title: SAMe Synthesis
mission: Maintain methionine adenosyltransferase capacity to convert methionine and ATP into SAMe, sustaining the methyl-donor pool used by downstream methyltransferases.
rationale: MAT methionine/ATP reaction is established, but aggregate dietary-protein identity and food delivery must be reconciled separately from SAM concentration and MAT flux. Unverified rows deferred, not rejected.

title: Methionine Cycle Flux
mission: Maintain balanced methionine-cycle flux so methionine availability, SAM-dependent methylation, homocysteine recycling and transsulfuration remain coordinated across changing physiological demand.
rationale: Cycle coordination overlaps its component reaction owners; concentration and enrichment are not integrated cycle flux. No new dietary lever inferred from pooled pathway claims.

title: Transsulfuration Pathway
mission: Divert homocysteine toward cysteine so methylation demand is balanced against sulfur amino-acid and redox needs.
rationale: PLP/serine transsulfuration capacity is retained historically; cystathionine/cysteine intermediates, sulphur supply and tissue-specific tracer interpretation need structured reconciliation. No extra-intake claim.

title: Glutathione Synthesis
mission: Build glutathione from sulfur amino acids so cellular antioxidant defence stays connected to one-carbon metabolism.
rationale: GCL/GSS substrate roles are supported in existing assessments. Sulphur-AA deprivation, combined NAC/glycine exposure and adequate-methionine cysteine null are distinct. Free cysteine versus cystine composition, glutamate/glutamine hydrolysis and ordinary-food substrate coverage remain unresolved; no fabricated food equivalence.

title: Phosphatidylcholine Formation
mission: Maintain phosphatidylcholine formation through PEMT methylation and the choline-based Kennedy pathway.
rationale: Kennedy and PEMT routes must remain separate; plasma PC/enrichment is not brain PC formation or total flux. Current route assessments preserved; additional form-specific dietary extraction deferred.

title: NF-kB Signalling Regulation
mission: Regulate NF-κB transcriptional tone so pro-inflammatory gene programmes do not fire excessively.
rationale: Upstream glutathione synthesis/repletion is not by itself dietary engagement of NF-kB. Existing IKK/redox and combined NAC/glycine results need PM-specific mediation and exposure attribution.

title: Gut-Derived Inflammatory Signalling
mission: Limit gut-derived endotoxin spillover so barrier dysfunction does not drive systemic inflammatory load.
rationale: Gut permeability, LPS exposure, glutathione supply and systemic cytokines are separate. Existing source cluster does not automatically establish a food regulator of systemic gut-derived inflammation.

title: Nrf2-Mediated Cellular Defence Regulation
mission: Regulate the expression of cellular defence genes in response to oxidative and electrophilic stress.
rationale: Cell mechanism and prepared-food exposure support bounded regulation; nasal targets are not direct brain efficacy. Mature-broccoli preparation join is held, while the specified disrupted-sprout source remains usable.

title: ROS Generation vs Clearance Balance
mission: Balance reactive oxygen species production and clearance so net oxidative pressure stays within tolerable limits.
rationale: Enzyme clearance capacity is distinguished from net ROS generation and from precursor ownership. Retain low-status context and do not add other minerals merely by enzyme membership.

title: Lipid Peroxidation Control
mission: Protect membrane fats from oxidative damage so vulnerable polyunsaturated fatty acids remain intact.
rationale: Owns lipid-peroxyl chain termination; regeneration belongs to PM6 and transcriptional regulation to Nrf2/NF-kB. Existing null/high-dose limits retained.

title: Antioxidant Network Recycling
mission: Regenerate vitamin and thiol antioxidants across networked systems so endogenous defence capacity is sustained.
rationale: Distinct regeneration operation retained. Broader thiol-network contribution remains an explicit coverage gap rather than a fabricated additional dietary admission.

title: Cytokine Network Modulation
mission: Tune downstream cytokine signalling intensity so inflammatory tone does not remain chronically elevated.
rationale: Prior bounded assessment reports null circulating-messenger findings and does not admit omega-3 from the adjacent mediator-biosynthesis PM. No lever established in that assessed corpus; not evidence of global absence.

title: Eicosanoid / SPM Balance
mission: Shift lipid mediator balance from pro-inflammatory eicosanoids toward pro-resolving signals that terminate inflammation.
rationale: Precursor substrate capacity retained; mediator formation and clinical termination of inflammation remain distinct. EPA/DHA are Direct to the owned biosynthetic operation, not direct food sources of SPMs.

title: Electron Transport Chain Function
mission: Sustain efficient electron transport so mitochondria generate ATP without excessive electron leakage.
rationale: ETC electron-transfer capacity is distinct from upstream NAD supply, fuel transport and biogenesis. FMN participant retained canonically but no separate unsupported direct-FMN food list is fabricated.

title: NAD⁺ Metabolism
mission: Maintain NAD⁺ availability so redox reactions and mitochondrial signalling stay adequately powered.
rationale: NAD supply is distinct from direct ETC electron transfer. Tryptophan route remains a conditional historical pathway but is not additionally abstracted without resolving tissue-specific contribution.

title: Creatine–Phosphocreatine Energy Buffering
mission: Enable rapid ATP buffering so high-energy-demand tissues can meet sudden metabolic spikes.
rationale: Buffer substrate identity is distinct from NAD or ETC capacity. A reviewed existing candidate admission is retained at the capacity ceiling; no high-dose brain protocol is prescribed.

title: ROS Production and Control
mission: Maintain balance between mitochondrial reactive oxygen species production and protective buffering to prevent redox damage.
rationale: No structured Scientific Findings; broad ROS-production/control scope overlaps BRS3 redox and mitochondrial protection. Generic antioxidant-food claims cannot pass a mechanism-specific gate.

title: Mitochondrial Protection (Redox Integrity)
mission: Preserve mitochondrial membrane and enzyme integrity so organelle function survives oxidative and metabolic strain.
rationale: No structured Scientific Findings; mitochondrial redox-integrity scope overlaps ROS control. Legacy antioxidant and CoQ10 claims need exact operation/source ownership before abstraction.

title: Carnitine-Mediated Fat Transport
mission: Enable long-chain fatty-acid transport into mitochondria so fat-derived ATP production can proceed.
rationale: No structured Scientific Findings. Carnitine transport capacity is not established by an ADHD outcome trial or generic fat oxidation; source-specific transport and dietary supply appraisal deferred.

title: Ketone Utilisation Capacity
mission: Enable mitochondrial ketone utilisation so alternative fuel is available when glucose conditions shift.
rationale: No structured Scientific Findings. Peripheral ketosis and low-carbohydrate patterns are not direct measurements of brain ketone oxidation. No automatic biochemical admission of a named diet.

title: Metabolic Fuel Switching
mission: Shape smooth transitions between glucose, fat, and ketone fuel pathways as physiological demand shifts.
rationale: No structured Scientific Findings. Whole-food patterns and mitophagy outcomes do not measure substrate-switching flexibility; legacy food claims held.

title: Mitochondrial Biogenesis
mission: Enable formation of new mitochondria so long-term energetic capacity can expand and adapt.
rationale: No structured Scientific Findings or current input assessment; exercise-dependent mitochondrial markers do not admit a food-driven biogenesis mechanism.

title: Gut Barrier / Tight Junction Integrity
mission: Maintain epithelial tight junction integrity and selective permeability at the gut lining.
rationale: Fermentation endpoints cannot stand in for tight-junction integrity. The van Trijp compartment/measurement and Pascale secondary-source corrections may recur in this PM; affected claims require source-level reconciliation, not a generic fibre-to-barrier conclusion.

title: LPS / Endotoxin Containment
mission: Limit host exposure to bacterial endotoxin and related inflammatory microbial products.
rationale: Chylomicron-associated LPS, permeability, LPS/LBP assays and bioactivity are distinct. Legacy meal/pattern inputs are ineligible for §3.1.1; nutrient/meal attribution and assay context require review.

title: Microbial Barrier–Immune Interface Support
mission: Support intestinal mucus maintenance and mucosal immune regulation through defined microbial activities.
rationale: Prior assessment bounds oligofructose-inulin and B. longum NCC2705 to tested mouse mucus endpoints. A strain is not generic fermented food; human permeability nulls and microbial context preserved.

title: Microbial Substrate-Processing Selection & Adaptation
mission: Adjust community substrate-processing capacity through resource competition and changes in microbial function.
rationale: Glycan selection/adaptation differs from SCFA production. Purified pea arabinan/citrus pectin and defined microbial communities cannot transfer effects to ordinary peas, citrus or every fibre source without separate evidence.

title: SCFA Production & Signalling
mission: Maintain short-chain fatty acid production and signalling that supports gut barrier and brain communication.
rationale: Reuse the accepted controlled PM5 correction, not a rerun. FOS/GOS remains held for review; inulin remains a candidate.

title: Polyphenol Biotransformation & Mitochondrial-Relevant Metabolite Generation
mission: Enable microbial activation of dietary polyphenols into bioactive metabolites.
rationale: Assess the existing ellagic-acid/urolithin pathway only; do not generalise across all polyphenols. Production of downstream metabolites and their efficacy belong to distinct claims.

title: Vagal / ENS Signalling Modulation
mission: Maintain gut-to-brain nerve signalling through the vagus nerve and enteric nervous system.
rationale: JB-1 mouse vagotomy evidence and a human null do not establish generic fermented-food vagal signalling. Nutrient enteroendocrine experiments do not justify increased sugar intake.

title: Neurotransmitter Precursor Biotransformation & Availability
mission: Maintain gut-side processing that shapes neurotransmitter precursor availability.
rationale: Tryptophan microbial routing, indole products and host precursor availability are distinct. Pectin cross-feeding is not proof of increased brain serotonin; pathway-specific exposure not rapidly verified.

title: Glucose Appearance Kinetics
mission: Shape the rate of post-meal glucose appearance so metabolic and neuroendocrine systems face manageable, predictable load.
rationale: Gastric delivery and tracer-estimated meal-glucose appearance are appropriate endpoints; ordinary glycaemia alone is not appearance flux. Other protocols remain individually unresolved until verified.

title: Glycaemic Variability Regulation
mission: Limit glycaemic volatility so post-prandial glucose swings do not create unnecessary metabolic and neuroendocrine stress.
rationale: Glucose variability is distinct from intestinal glucose appearance and insulin-stimulated disposal. Retain selected CGM-tested practices; no inferred neuron or ADHD improvement.

title: Insulin Sensitivity & Glucose Disposal
mission: Sustain insulin-sensitive glucose disposal so post-meal glucose clears efficiently without prolonged metabolic strain.
rationale: Clamp-measured exercise/weight-loss effects and rat magnesium-depletion effects require separate dose/population assessment. No generic food insulin-sensitivity claim inferred from weight change.

title: Cortisol Rhythm Regulation
mission: Maintain diurnal cortisol amplitude and phase so morning activation and evening downshift stay well timed.
rationale: Combined sleep/light/meal misalignment does not isolate meal timing or cortisol mediation. Prebiotic awakening-response data do not establish whole-day rhythm correction.

title: Circadian Feeding & Light–Dark Entrainment
rationale: Retired compatibility/redirect page has no active PM identity; not counted in active PM inventory.

title: Sympathetic Activation & Parasympathetic Recovery
mission: Maintain autonomic flexibility by shifting cleanly from sympathetic activation back into parasympathetic recovery.
rationale: Skin conductance and HRV recovery are bounded autonomic proxies. Meditation/stress interventions need protocol-specific attribution; no dietary relationship inferred.

title: Vagal Tone / HRV Regulation
mission: Sustain vagal tone so heart-rate-variability-linked recovery signalling remains robust under repeated stress exposure.
rationale: Respiratory HRV effects and capsule omega-3 HRV findings require separate interpretation; HRV is not a direct universal vagal-tone measure or a fish efficacy result.

title: Metabolic Inflammation & Adipose Stress Signalling
mission: Limit metabolic-inflammatory signalling from adipose stress so whole-body resource allocation is not overloaded.
rationale: Explicit architectural-review exclusion: mission and ownership unresolved. No dietary abstraction, new admission or Stage 2A/2B rebuild authorised for this PM.

title: Stress-Induced Appetite / Reward Drive Modulation
mission: Shape stress-linked appetite and reward drive so food-seeking behaviour stays proportionate to genuine need.
rationale: Subjective appetite/stress-eating outcomes do not by themselves establish neural reward-pathway engagement. No food timing or ingredient claim inferred.
